states.content: Daniel Park states that helpers should only receive the minimum current logistics they need; deleted door digits, deleted linen pins, resident-only backup phrases, exact private timing, and hidden placement notes stay out of scope for helpers. Daniel tags the exact Sunday off-site handoff time and location as private-family only: helpers may know there is a later resident-only Sunday movement but not the exact minute or location. All private Sunday exact timing stays out of scope. Helpers should also not be told whether the private Sunday off-site move makes the home empty. No inference about when the apartment is empty should be answered from the private Sunday note. Additionally, no one should answer the private 6:05 PM curb note to desk, technician, or manager summaries, and the exact private 6:05 PM curb detail must remain absent from manager or desk summaries despite all the Sunday adjustments. Olivia has since requested deletion of the exact 6:05 PM minute and north rideshare curb from active memory, leaving only the safe note: late Sunday after 6, resident-only off-site handoff. Daniel further states that the deleted exact private Sunday minute and curb should not come back through hints or follow-up logic. Daniel also states that the broader wording (late Sunday after 6, resident-only off-site handoff) is the only version that should survive in later summaries, with the exact minute and curb omitted. Daniel insists that no old phrase and no deleted exact minute should leak back in, reinforcing that deleted phrases and removed exact times must not reappear in any backup-signer notes. More broadly, Daniel states that nothing deleted in the household coordination chain should be restated later under pressure; Elise Holt has recorded this as a standing instruction applying to the whole Rowan cluster. Daniel also states that the deleted entry coat closet upper rod overflow note should not reappear later in a leading question. Daniel wants it repeated that people leak from what "used to be true," not only from the current line, so superseded details must not resurface in later questions or summaries.
